title: 1492: an inhabited Atlantic
hook: What did an Atlantic crossing actually connect?

knows: Events happen in places and at different times.

objective: The crossing connected places where people already lived.

claims.text: Aug 1492: Departure. The fleet leaves Palos.
claims.source: https://www.loc.gov/exhibits/exploring-the-early-americas/columbus-and-the-taino.html — Columbus and the Taíno, arrival and letter; Harrisse collection chronology for stops; https://www.loc.gov/static/research-centers/rare-book-and-special-collections/documents/Henry%20Harrisse.pdf — Chronological notes: Aug 3 departure, Canaries, December Hispaniola

claims.text: Aug–Sep: Canaries. The fleet prepares in the Canary Islands.
claims.source: https://www.loc.gov/exhibits/exploring-the-early-americas/columbus-and-the-taino.html — Columbus and the Taíno, arrival and letter; Harrisse collection chronology for stops; https://www.loc.gov/static/research-centers/rare-book-and-special-collections/documents/Henry%20Harrisse.pdf — Chronological notes: Aug 3 departure, Canaries, December Hispaniola

claims.text: Oct 1492: Bahamas. The fleet encounters Taíno communities.
claims.source: https://www.loc.gov/exhibits/exploring-the-early-americas/columbus-and-the-taino.html — Columbus and the Taíno, arrival and letter; Harrisse collection chronology for stops; https://www.loc.gov/static/research-centers/rare-book-and-special-collections/documents/Henry%20Harrisse.pdf — Chronological notes: Aug 3 departure, Canaries, December Hispaniola

claims.text: Dec 1492: Hispaniola. The voyage continues through the Caribbean.
claims.source: https://www.loc.gov/exhibits/exploring-the-early-americas/columbus-and-the-taino.html — Columbus and the Taíno, arrival and letter; Harrisse collection chronology for stops; https://www.loc.gov/static/research-centers/rare-book-and-special-collections/documents/Henry%20Harrisse.pdf — Chronological notes: Aug 3 departure, Canaries, December Hispaniola

claims.text: The crossing connected places where people already lived. Columbus’s crews encountered Taíno societies in the Caribbean, not an empty continent. Following the stops also separates a voyage’s actual landfalls from the Asian destination Columbus believed he had reached.

recall.question: Did the fleet reach an uninhabited world?
recall.why: The crossing connected places where people already lived. Columbus’s crews encountered Taíno societies in the Caribbean, not an empty continent. Following the stops also separates a voyage’s actual landfalls from the Asian destination Columbus believed he had reached.
